grow_divide.doc:
Growth/division using the adder model (Taheri-Araghi et al. 2015).

Each cell:
  * has its own per-cell α (h⁻¹) and Δ (added length, µm)
  * grows exponentially in length: L(t+dt) = L(t) · exp(α · dt)
  * divides when L >= L_birth + Δ
  * daughters get length (L_div / 2) · LogNormal(1, division_noise_cv)
    and fresh α, Δ samples

_contract.summary: Adder-model growth & division (Taheri-Araghi et al. 2015) — each cell adds a ~constant increment of size per cycle regardless of birth size.

inputs.agents: Cells; per cell: location (µm), length (µm), radius (µm), mass (pg), angle (rad), velocity (µm/s).

outputs.agents: Cells growing at alpha_mean_per_h (1/h); divide after adding delta_mean (µm), with CV noise. Nutrient-limited via Monod (nutrient µM, Km µM).

assumptions: Added size per cycle (delta) is birth-size-independent (the 'adder' principle).

multibody.doc:
2D rigid-body physics for colonies — a pymunk space that integrates
rod-shaped cells, soft multi-segment cells, and circular particles under
collisions, damping, jitter, optional gravity/adhesion, and chamber walls.

Its structured ``contract`` (with per-port units) is assigned at the bottom
of this module alongside the other process contracts.

_contract.summary: 2D rigid-body physics for the colony — steps a pymunk space so cells grow, push apart, and reorient under collisions, damping, and jitter.

inputs.segment_cells: Rod-shaped rigid cells — per cell: location (µm), length (µm), radius (µm), mass (pg), angle (rad), velocity (µm/s).
inputs.bending_cells: Soft multi-segment capsule cells joined by rotary springs — per cell: location (µm), length (µm), radius (µm), mass (pg), angle (rad), velocity (µm/s).
inputs.circle_particles: Circular particles (e.g. EPS) — location (µm), radius (µm), mass (pg).

outputs.segment_cells: Rod cells after one physics step — position (µm) / angle (rad) advanced by forces + collisions.
outputs.bending_cells: Bending cells after one physics step (segment poses updated).

assumptions: Overdamped motion (velocity damping/s, gravity off by default); `substeps` sub-steps per update; rectangular chamber of side env_size (µm) with walls of wall_thickness (µm).

multibody_viz.doc: Streaming animated-GIF renderer matching the test-suite GIF style. Per ``update(state)``: 1. Merge cells + particles into one layer, stamp the static field onto the frame so the heatmap overlay renders every tick. 2. ``GifRenderer.draw_frame(...)`` → PIL Image; append to internal ``self._frames``. 3. Quantize all accumulated frames (MEDIANCUT, 256 colors) and encode as an animated GIF in-memory (``disposal=2``, ``optimize=False`` — same pattern as ``simulation_to_gif``). 4. Return ``{'html': ''}``. Performance: re-encoding the GIF on every tick is O(n²) in step count. For dashboard test runs (2–50 steps) this is sub-second; for longer runs the ``max_frames`` cap drops oldest frames FIFO to bound memory and encode time.

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type
